input.comment: [Playbook] We accept Client's existing right to terminate on notice, but it should run on 30 days' notice and be free of penalty, with any prepaid fees refunded pro rata for the period after termination.

ops.oldText: until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
ops.newText: until the effective date of termination specified in a written notice of Client's election to terminate this Agreement for convenience, which Client may give at any time on not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice and without penalty or early-termination charge, and TrueLink shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.summary: Cap renewal price increases and add a renewal reminder
input.comment: [Playbook] The 12-month renewal term and 30-day non-renewal window work for us; we have added a cap on renewal price increases (lesser of CPI and 3%) and a 60-day renewal reminder so the opt-out is meaningful.

ops.oldText: unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year.
ops.newText: unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year. TrueLink shall notify Client of any upcoming renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term, and fees for any renewal term shall not increase by more than the lesser of the change in CPI over the preceding twelve (12) months and three percent (3%).

input.summary: Add affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for Client and a reasonableness standard on consent
input.comment: [Playbook] We must be able to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets without consent, and consent to other assignments should not be unreasonably withheld; TrueLink should not assign to a Client competitor.

ops.oldText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
ops.newText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or, in the case of Client, to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or equity. TrueLink shall not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Client, and no change of control of Client shall give TrueLink any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.

input.summary: Confirm Client ownership of Client data and Support Services work product, with a licence-back of embedded TrueLink IP
input.comment: [Playbook] We own what we put in and what we pay for: Client Content, Client Intellectual Property, borrower/applicant data and the work product of the Support Services should remain ours, with a perpetual royalty-free licence to any TrueLink IP embedded in that work product. TrueLink keeps ownership of the Interface itself.

ops.oldText: d. Ownership. Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface.
ops.newText: d. Ownership. Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface. Client retains all right, title and interest in and to the Client Content, Client Intellectual Property and all borrower, loan applicant and other Client data submitted to or generated through the Interface or the Web Site, and nothing herein assigns or transfers any such rights to TrueLink. All results and work product of the Support Services prepared for Client are the property of Client, and TrueLink hereby assigns such work product to Client and grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense any TrueLink Intellectual Property embedded therein. No jointly owned intellectual property is created under this Agreement.

input.summary: Extend the licence to Client affiliates and contractors and make it transferable to a successor
input.comment: [Playbook] The licence must cover our affiliates and the contractors and correspondent brokers acting on our behalf (as contemplated by the recitals) and must transfer to a successor in an M&A transaction; it should be terminable only in accordance with this Agreement, not at TrueLink's discretion.

ops.oldText: a. Grant. TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement.
ops.newText: a. Grant. TrueLink hereby grants to Client, its affiliates and its contractors and correspondent brokers acting on its behalf a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement. The license is transferable to a successor of Client by merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, and may not be revoked or suspended except upon termination of this Agreement in accordance with its terms.

input.summary: Add a TrueLink performance/conformance warranty with a real remedy and carve it out of the disclaimer
input.comment: [Playbook] TrueLink's only warranty today is Y2K readiness, and the disclaimer leaves us without any conformance warranty. We have added a professional-services warranty and a 90-day conformance warranty with re-performance, repair/replacement or refund as the remedy.

ops.text: TrueLink further warrants that (a) the Hosting Services and Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, the Interface and each deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation; (c) it will comply with applicable law in performing hereunder; and (d) the Interface and any deliverable will be free of viruses, worms, Trojan horses and other malicious code. Client's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at TrueLink's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming services or deliverable. The express warranties in this Section are not limited or excluded by any disclaimer in this Agreement.

input.summary: Insert a Vendor insurance provision
input.comment: [Playbook] TrueLink hosts our web site and handles borrower credit data, so standard cover is required: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M and cyber/privacy USD 5M, with certificates on request.

ops.text: 31. INSURANCE. TrueLink shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and workers' compensation insurance as required by law. TrueLink shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

input.summary: Limit the monthly minimum fees to the current term and make them reducible
input.comment: [Playbook] We do not take minimum commitments without an exit. The monthly minimums should apply only during the current 12-month term, be reducible on 30 days' notice, and cease on termination as a true-up rather than a penalty.

ops.oldText: (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services)
ops.newText: (but, during the then-current twelve (12) month term only, not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services, which minimums Client may reduce on thirty (30) days' written notice, shall be trued up rather than applied as a penalty, and shall not accrue for any period after the effective date of termination)

input.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance, data return and deletion certification
input.comment: [Playbook] On exit we need our data back and help migrating: up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Client data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (a) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Client Content, Client data and borrower and loan applicant data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.
input.rationale: The only cap is one-way: it protects TrueLink alone (Client's liability, including under its broad Section 12(a) indemnity, is unlimited) and it applies only to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 rather than the whole agreement. There is no USD floor, no mutual exclusion of consequential damages, no carve-out for confidentiality/data-security or indemnification, and no confirmation that Client's payment obligations sit outside the cap. We made the cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000 with the standard Excluded Claims.

input.quote: TrueLink shall indemnify and hold Client harmless, its affiliates, directors, officers, employees, agents and licensors harmless from and against all claims, actions, expenses, losses, and liabilities, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising from or relating to any
input.rationale: TrueLink's indemnity is limited to its own breach or failure to perform and contains no third-party IP-infringement indemnity for the Interface or Hosting Services, no breach-of-law, data-breach or misconduct coverage — while Client's indemnity in 12(a) is very broad (including claims "without regard to any knowledge limitation"). We added the standard Vendor indemnity limbs; the asymmetry with 12(a) should also be revisited.

input.quote: Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Client — Section 2(a) expressly preserves our freedom to build or buy competing software. However, Section 8(d) makes the Credit Data licence "subject to the limitations set forth in and in accordance with the Non-Competition Agreement", an instrument not defined or attached here; we should review that agreement to confirm it imposes no restraint on Client's business before signing off. No redline to this document.

input.quote: Subject to the foregoing, Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface.
input.rationale: The licence itself is non-exclusive, but Section 3(i) obliges Client to source a credit report from TrueLink for every borrower underwritten through the Interface, with no performance-based exit — effectively a sole-source requirement for the term (1 year, auto-renewing). We narrowed it to Interface transactions and added an exit where TrueLink misses the Section 3 service levels or cannot supply the data.

input.quote: TrueLink agrees that the costs for any Hosting Services will not increase for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement and that rates charged for Hosting Services will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party.
input.rationale: The only most-favoured-nation undertaking runs in our favour (TrueLink's Hosting Services rates may not exceed those charged to any other party). No MFN obligation burdens Client, so no redline; we keep this clause as drafted.

input.quote: 8. COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT
input.rationale: We found no non-solicitation, no-hire or employee-inducement restriction anywhere in the Agreement (Client covenants in Section 8 and the confidentiality provisions in Section 10 contain none). Our preferred position — no non-solicit on Customer — is met, so no redline.

input.quote: TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Client does have a convenience exit (service continues to the end of the following month, i.e. 30–60 days) and TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right, so we are within our fallback. It falls short of the preferred position because the notice period is indeterminate (up to two months) and there is no refund of prepaid fees; we set 30 days' notice without penalty and added a pro-rata refund.

input.quote: This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year.
input.rationale: The renewal term (12 months) and the 30-day non-renewal window meet our preferred position, but the price protection in Section 6 expires after the first year, so renewal pricing is uncapped and there is no renewal reminder. We added a 60-day reminder and capped renewal increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

input.quote: Any and all disputes between the parties that cannot be settled by mutual agreement shall be resolved solely and exclusively in the state or federal courts located within San Luis Obispo County, California, and each party consents to the jurisdiction of such courts and irrevocably waives any objections thereto
input.rationale: California law with exclusive jurisdiction of California state and federal courts, and no arbitration, falls within our accepted fallback list. The only comment is venue in TrueLink's home county (San Luis Obispo) rather than a neutral or Client-side venue such as Orange County; we would raise that as a trade only if other points are conceded, so no redline here.

input.quote: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
input.rationale: Assignment is mutual and has an affiliate carve-out, but there is no M&A/successor carve-out for Client and consent is unqualified (TrueLink could withhold it arbitrarily on a sale of our business). We added the successor carve-out, a "not unreasonably withheld" standard, a bar on assignment to a Client competitor, and confirmation that a Client change of control gives TrueLink no termination or re-pricing right.

input.quote: Client hereby grants to TrueLink the nonexclusive worldwide right and license to use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit, upload, display, copy and store Credit Data subject to the limitations set forth in and in accordance with the Non-Competition Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 2(d) confirms only TrueLink's ownership; nothing confirms that Client owns its borrower/applicant data or the work product of the Support Services, while the TrueLink Intellectual Property definition sweeps in everything "associated with the Interface" (including customizations we pay for) and Section 8(d) grants TrueLink a worldwide right to resell and exploit our borrowers' Credit Data. We added a Client data/work-product ownership sentence with a licence-back of embedded TrueLink IP and a no-joint-ownership statement; TrueLink keeps the Interface.

input.quote: a. Grant. TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement.
input.rationale: The grant runs to Client only — affiliates and the correspondent brokers/contractors contemplated by the recitals are not covered (and Section 8(c) limits access to Client's own officers, employees and agents), there is no successor transferability, and Section 13 terminates the licence "promptly" on certain Client breaches with no cure period. We extended the grant to affiliates and contractors, added successor transfer, and limited revocation to termination under the Agreement.

input.quote: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
input.rationale: There is no audit, inspection or usage-verification right running against Client; the only information rights run in our favour (supporting documentation for charges) and the access reference in Section 9 is limited to letting TrueLink make its own Y2K repairs. Preferred position met, no redline.

input.quote: Invoices will be paid within 15 days of receipt.
input.rationale: No liquidated damages, penalty interest, stipulated penalties or termination charges are payable by Client — the anti-spam covenant in Section 7 and the enforcement right in Section 8(f) carry no monetary penalty, and there is no early-termination fee. The monthly minimum fees are addressed separately under MINCOMMIT. No redline.

input.quote: EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, TRUELINK DISCLAIMS ANY AND ALL EXPENSES WARRANTIES, WARRANTIES OF FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FOR ANY MATTER RELATING TO THE ACCURACY OR COMPLETENESS, OR TIMING OF TRANSMISSION OF ANY DATA SUBMITTED THROUGH THE INTERFACE OR TO OR FROM THE WEB SITE.
input.rationale: TrueLink's only express warranty is Y2K date handling (Section 9); the Hosting and Support Services carry no conformance warranty, no compliance-with-law or malicious-code warranty and no remedy, while Section 3 obligations are "reasonable commercial efforts" and Section 12 disclaims the implied warranties. We inserted a workmanlike-performance and 90-day conformance warranty with repair/re-perform/refund, expressly carved out of the disclaimer.

input.quote: 30. FORCE MAJEURE. TrueLink will be excused from delays in performing or from failing to perform its obligations under this Agreement to the extent the delays or failures result from causes beyond the reasonable control or TrueLink.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance provision at all, even though TrueLink hosts our web site and processes borrower credit data. We inserted a short insurance section (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation) with certificates on request; E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is our fallback.

input.quote: (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services)
input.rationale: Section 5(a) imposes monthly minimum fees regardless of usage, and Section 6 removes any right to contest them, on a term that renews automatically for successive years — a take-or-pay with no reduction mechanism. We limited the minimums to the current 12-month term, made them reducible on 30 days' notice, and confirmed they are trued up rather than applied as a penalty and do not accrue after termination.

input.quote: If Client decides to discontinue Hosting Service, Client is responsible for arranging for a new hosting environment within 60 days.
input.rationale: Exit is handled only by placing the migration burden on Client (new name server in 30 days, new hosting environment in 60 days); there is no transition-assistance obligation, no return of our data in a usable format and no deletion certification, despite TrueLink holding the Web Site, borrower data and daily backups. We inserted the standard transition/data-return paragraph in the termination section.

content.text:
All 18 playbook rules have been reviewed and submitted. Summary of our position:

**Critical**
- **LOL-CAP** (deviation): cap protects TrueLink only, and only for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11; our liability is unlimited. Made mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1M, added consequential-damages exclusion and Excluded Claims.
- **INDEMN** (deviation): TrueLink indemnifies only for its own breach — no IP-infringement, breach-of-law, data-breach or misconduct limbs, against a very broad Client indemnity in 12(a). Added the Vendor limbs.
- **IP** (deviation): no confirmation we own our borrower data or Support Services work product, and 8(d) lets TrueLink resell Credit Data. Added ownership/licence-back and no-joint-ownership language.

**High**
- **LICENSE** (deviation): grant excludes affiliates/contractors and successors, and terminates without cure. **ASSIGN** (deviation): no M&A carve-out, unqualified consent. **T4C** (deviation): exit exists but indeterminate notice and no refund. **EXCLUSIVITY** (deviation): 3(i) requires every credit report from TrueLink with no performance exit. **NONCOMPETE** (needs review): none in this document, but the referenced "Non-Competition Agreement" must be reviewed. **LD** (compliant).

**Medium/low**
- **RENEWAL**, **MINCOMMIT**, **WARRANTY**, **TRANSITION**, **INSURANCE**: redlined as above. **MFN**, **NOSOLICIT**, **AUDIT**, **GOVLAW** (California law/courts within fallback): compliant, no redline.

system.text:
You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Client-side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the TrueLink Interface, Hosting and Support Services Agreement

## Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of Exhibit 10.4 and marked up the document. The commercial architecture is workable, but the risk allocation is materially one-sided in TrueLink's favour on the three issues we treat as non-negotiable: indemnification, ownership of our data and work product, and limitation of liability.

- **Indemnity (§ 12)** runs essentially one way. TrueLink indemnifies only for its own breach or failure to perform, with no IP-infringement, breach-of-law, data-breach or misconduct cover, while our indemnity in 12(a) is very broad and applies "without regard to any knowledge limitation."
- **Ownership (§ 2)** confirms only TrueLink's rights. The "TrueLink Intellectual Property" definition sweeps in everything "associated with the Interface" — including customisations we pay for — and § 8(d) grants TrueLink a worldwide right to resell and exploit our borrowers' Credit Data.
- **Liability (§ 12)** is capped for TrueLink alone, and only as to §§ 3, 4, 7 and 11. Our exposure, including under the broad 12(a) indemnity, is unlimited, with no floor, no mutual consequential-damages exclusion and no Excluded Claims.
- Secondary but significant: the § 3(i) sole-source obligation to order every credit report from TrueLink with no performance exit; monthly take-or-pay minimums that renew automatically (§§ 5–6); no TrueLink performance warranty beyond Y2K (§ 9); no transition assistance or data return on exit; and no insurance provision at all.
- Several areas already meet our preferred position and require no redline: no audit rights against us, no non-solicitation, no liquidated damages or early-termination fee, an MFN that runs in our favour, and California law/courts with no arbitration.
- One open diligence item: § 8(d) subjects the Credit Data licence to a "Non-Competition Agreement" that is neither defined nor attached. We cannot clear the non-compete question without seeing it.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position taken |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No TrueLink IP-infringement, breach-of-law, data-breach or misconduct indemnity; our 12(a) indemnity is far broader. We added the standard Vendor limbs and flagged the asymmetry. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | Only TrueLink's ownership is confirmed; § 8(d) permits resale of borrower Credit Data. We added Client ownership of data and Support Services work product, a licence-back of embedded TrueLink IP and a no-joint-ownership statement. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | One-way cap limited to §§ 3, 4, 7 and 11; our liability unlimited. We made the cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000 with standard Excluded Claims. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | § 3(i) requires a TrueLink credit report for every borrower underwritten through the Interface, with no exit. We narrowed it to Interface transactions and added an exit for missed § 3 service levels or failure to supply data. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | Grant covers Client only (§ 8(c) limits access to our officers, employees and agents), is non-transferable, and § 13 terminates it "promptly" with no cure period. We extended it to affiliates and contractors, added successor transfer and limited revocation to termination. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No M&A/successor carve-out and consent is unqualified. We added the successor carve-out, a "not unreasonably withheld" standard, a bar on assignment to our competitors, and confirmation that a change of control gives TrueLink no termination or re-pricing right. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | We have a convenience exit (within fallback), but notice is indeterminate (30–60 days) and prepaid fees are non-refundable. We set 30 days' notice without penalty plus pro-rata refund. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Needs review | § 2 LICENSE. | No restraint in this document (§ 2(a) preserves our freedom to build or buy competing software), but § 8(d) incorporates an undefined, unattached "Non-Competition Agreement." No redline pending review. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No liquidated damages, penalty interest or early-termination fee; § 7 anti-spam covenant and § 8(f) enforcement right carry no monetary penalty. No redline. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments | Deviation | § 5 COMPENSATION. | § 5(a) monthly minimums regardless of usage, § 6 removes any right to contest, on an auto-renewing term. We limited minimums to the current 12-month term, made them reducible on 30 days' notice, and confirmed true-up (not penalty) treatment with no post-termination accrual. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Only express warranty is Y2K date handling (§ 9); § 3 is "reasonable commercial efforts" and § 12 disclaims implied warranties. We added workmanlike-performance and 90-day conformance warranties with repair/re-perform/refund, carved out of the disclaimer. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Exit places the whole migration burden on us (30-day name server, 60-day hosting) with no transition assistance, data return or deletion certification, though TrueLink holds the Web Site, borrower data and backups. We inserted the standard paragraph. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | 12-month renewal and 30-day window are acceptable, but § 6 price protection lapses after year one. We added a 60-day reminder and capped increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No audit, inspection or usage-verification right against us; § 9 access is limited to TrueLink's own Y2K repairs. No redline. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No non-solicit, no-hire or inducement restriction anywhere in the Agreement. No redline. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | The only MFN runs in our favour (Hosting Services rates may not exceed those charged to any other party). Keep as drafted. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | California law, exclusive California state/federal courts, no arbitration — within our fallback. Venue in TrueLink's home county (San Luis Obispo) is a trade item only. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No insurance provision at all, despite TrueLink hosting our web site and processing borrower credit data. We inserted CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M and workers' compensation, certificates on request. |

## Walk-away items

We should not sign without movement on the following:

1. **Vendor indemnity (§ 12).** A third-party IP-infringement indemnity for the Interface and Hosting Services, plus breach-of-law, data-breach and misconduct limbs, and rebalancing of our "without regard to any knowledge limitation" indemnity in 12(a).
2. **Ownership and use of our data (§ 2; § 8(d)).** Express confirmation that we own our borrower/applicant data and the Support Services work product, and removal or tight limitation of TrueLink's worldwide right to resell and exploit our borrowers' Credit Data.
3. **Mutual liability cap with carve-outs (§ 12).** Unlimited Client exposure sitting beneath a one-way, section-specific cap is not acceptable. We need mutuality, agreement-wide application, the USD floor, a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and carve-outs for confidentiality/data security and indemnification.
4. **Sole-source obligation (§ 3(i)).** A performance-based exit is required; a term-long, auto-renewing requirement to buy every credit report from TrueLink with no service-level remedy is unacceptable alongside the § 5(a) minimums.

## Next steps

1. Send our redline to TrueLink with the four walk-away items identified as gating, and the § 12 cap, indemnity and § 2 ownership language marked as non-negotiable in substance.
2. Request the **Non-Competition Agreement** referenced in § 8(d) before we clear the non-compete rule; we cannot confirm the absence of a restraint on our business until we have reviewed it.
3. Table the secondary deviations as a package trade: § 5(a)/§ 6 minimums and renewal pricing, licence scope for affiliates and contractors, assignment/change-of-control, the 30-day convenience notice with pro-rata refund, the performance warranty, transition assistance and data return, and the insurance section (fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).
4. Hold the San Luis Obispo venue point in reserve as a concession we can accept if the § 12 items land.
5. Confirm with the business the expected monthly credit-report volumes so we can size the reducible minimum under § 5(a) before the next exchange."}
